name: LIECHTENSTEIN

flag.title: Blue & Red Crown
flag.note: Crown added 1937 after Haiti flag mix-up

lead: Liechtenstein is one of the world's tiniest countries, between Switzerland and Austria. A real prince lives in a hilltop castle. It has soaring Alpine peaks, no army and no airport. It also has famous stamps.

sections.geography: A pocket kingdom in the Alps
sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: The broad Rhine River marks Liechtenstein's western edge. The jagged Rätikon Alps rise to the east. The country is only 26 km from tip to tip.
The flat Rhine valley gives way to steep forests, alpine meadows and snowy peaks. The lowest point is the Rhine at 430 m. The highest is Grauspitz at 2,599 m.
animals: Chamois, nimble goat-like animals, leap between cliffs on the Alpine slopes. Ibex, whistling marmots and red deer live here too. Marmots fatten up for winter.
Golden eagles circle on broad wings above the treeline. Over 150 bird species have been recorded here. In autumn, cattle wearing flowers parade down from summer pastures in the Alpabzug.
culture: Liechtensteiners speak an Alemannic German dialect. On National Day, 15 August, the Prince opens his castle gates. He invites every citizen to a garden party.
In autumn, people harvest grapes for Pinot Noir on sunny Rhine valley slopes. This is called Wimmlete. Operetta societies in Balzers and Vaduz have staged musicals for over 80 years.
history: The principality began on 23 January 1719. Holy Roman Emperor Charles VI united tiny Vaduz and Schellenberg. He named them after the Liechtenstein family.
Napoleon ended the Holy Roman Empire in 1806. Liechtenstein joined his Rhine Confederation. Full independence came in 1866. The country abolished its tiny army in 1868 and has stayed neutral.
wows: Liechtenstein and Uzbekistan are the only doubly landlocked countries.
Its 10 Olympic medals are all in Alpine skiing.
The Princely House is said to be Europe's wealthiest royal family.
Liechtenstein has no airport, so visitors arrive by road or train.
Postage stamps are a real export, and collectors hunt them worldwide.
In 1936, officials saw their flag matched Haiti's and added a gold crown.
Seven of the 10 medals came from one family, the Wenzels.

myths.fact: They come from the Black Forest in Germany.

myths.myth: Mountain tops are cold because they are nearer to space
myths.fact: Air thins with height and holds less heat. It cools about 6 °C for every 1,000 m you climb.
